stem:
The diagram shows Harsh aiming a concave mirror at the Sun so parallel sunlight rays meet on a dry leaf held near the focus.

Why can a bright hot spot form on the leaf?

options.text: The concave mirror concentrates the reflected sunlight into a small spot on the leaf.
The concave mirror spreads the parallel rays evenly across the leaf, so no small hot spot is needed.
Any shiny object concentrates sunlight the same way even if its surface is flat.
The bright spot forms only because the leaf looks darker than the mirror in the diagram.

teacher.key_rationale: A concave mirror concentrates reflected parallel sunlight into a small bright hot spot. Spreading the rays drops the focusing condition; treating any flat shiny surface the same over-widens the rule; judging from leaf colour is a surface feature.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote converging-lens ray diagram into a concave mirror focusing parallel rays onto a leaf.
